payload.title: The restatement invariant has narrow recall: finding-id-grammar.spec.ts matches only the shapes the repository carried at the base, so a new fixed-digit finding-id regex of another shape passes it
evidence: tests/invariants/finding-id-grammar.spec.ts:189-227 (DIGITS, RESTATEMENT_SHAPES and restatementsIn: the four-severity alternation, a [A-Z0-9]+ classifier, the ORPHAN heading form, padStart(3, parseInt(...slice(-3)))
tests/invariants/finding-id-grammar.spec.ts:249-291 (the self-test lists only sites the base carried)
tests/invariants/finding-id-grammar.spec.ts:25-29 (the header says the shapes cover the domain-classifier-sequence segments; the classifier segment is only [A-Z0-9]+)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md architectural-solution hierarchy tier 3: a detector that only recognises yesterday's spellings does not make the next spelling detectable
payload.notes: Close condition: The detector flags any regex literal or RegExp source that joins a classifier-like segment ([A-Z]+, [A-Z0-9]+, a severity word list) to a fixed digit class (\d{n} or [0-9]{n}, n >= 3) with a hyphen, and the slice(-3) and padStart(3) forms outside the present shapes. The self-test lists the seven lines of the probe and each is detected, the NOT_RESTATEMENTS lines (F-NNN, DEBT, the NIT dialect, an unrelated counter) stay clean, and the scan of tools/, tests/ and aria-kernel/ is clean or each new hit is decided.
